Ella —

Appreciate the clear summary. Short answer: yes — we can do both, and we typically handle this through a billing-lane configuration plus a small amendment for the credit guardrail. High-level proposal attached. Key points: 

- Invoice routing: we can route line-items to different legal entities based on a region tag (you can push region at request time, or we can infer from billing address). That allows the EU entity to be invoiced and show VAT as charged/collected.
- Monthly account-level credit cap: we keep a unified consumption ledger and enforce a total exposure cap. Individual invoices go to the appropriate entity but the cap is enforced at the account level.
- Triggered lane (staged schedule): when month consumption > $120k, we switch to a 45-day staggered invoice lane rather than single immediate invoicing. During the triggered period we can: 
  * Hold additional provisioning if exposure exceeds an agreed backstop;
  * Emit internal reconciliation reports (CSV) for your finance team;
  * Offer a one-time short-term credit buffer (subject to guarantee/PO or a deposit) which is captured in an amendment.

Attachment: triggered-invoice-lanes-v1.pdf — one-page diagram + sample CSV.

On the legal side: this is usually a short billing exhibit + a credit amendment (1 page each). Grace and Marissa — can you confirm the internal credit/backstop options (deposit vs. surety vs. PO) and whether a rolling 45-day buffer is acceptable from finance? If we need bespoke language, legal will prepare a short exhibit.

Next steps I recommend: 
1) Marissa to outline acceptable exposures and whether we require collateral;
2) I send a redline-friendly draft exhibit to Ella;
3) Grace will configure a test lane for your pilot usage next week.
